chunks: Say: "The truth has come, and falsehood had neither precedence nor will reappear."

key_terms.الْبَاطِلُ: Falsehood (that which is void or temporary)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says falsehood neither preceded nor will return?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Saba, this verse serves as a decisive proclamation of the Prophet Muhammad's mission, affirming that divine truth has irrevocably supplanted idolatry and falsehood. Shia exegetes often highlight the grammatical structure to emphasize that falsehood was never a permanent rival but merely a transient state, ensuring the eternal supremacy of Haqq. This assurance reinforces the believer's confidence in the ultimate victory of justice over oppression, a core tenet in Shia eschatology.
